**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown. Time yourself: aim for about 30 minutes
(roughly 2 minutes per question, the same pace as the full exam). The strong-acid and strong-base lists are **not** provided: work from memory.

**Answer sheet.** Use the bubble answer sheet (`CHEM1301/exam-prep/answer-sheet/answer-sheet.pdf`), rows 1–15.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** According to the Arrhenius definition used in this course, an **acid** is a substance that:

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ always contains oxygen\
b)\ produces hydroxide ions (OH^−^) when it is dissolved in water\
c)\ forms a precipitate when mixed with a base\
d)\ gains electrons from a metal\
e)\ produces H^+^ ions (protons) when it is dissolved in water

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ HCl and H~2~SO~4~\
b)\ HC~2~H~3~O~2~ and HNO~3~\
c)\ HF and HCl\
d)\ HNO~3~ and HNO~2~\
e)\ H~3~PO~4~ and H~2~SO~4~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

\needspace{9\baselineskip}

**3.** What **salt** forms when sulfuric acid reacts completely with potassium hydroxide? H~2~SO~4~(aq) + 2KOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ ? + 2H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ K~2~SO~4~\
b)\ KSO~4~\
c)\ KOH\
d)\ K(SO~4~)~2~\
e)\ H~2~O

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**4.** Hydrochloric acid reacts with potassium hydroxide: HCl(aq) + KOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ KCl(aq) + H~2~O(l). What is the **net ionic** equation?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ HCl(aq) + OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ Cl^−^(aq) + H~2~O(l)\
b)\ K^+^(aq) + Cl^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ KCl(s)\
c)\ HCl(aq) + KOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ KCl(aq) + H~2~O(l)\
d)\ H^+^(aq) + Cl^−^(aq) + K^+^(aq) + OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ K^+^(aq) + Cl^−^(aq) + H~2~O(l)\
e)\ H^+^(aq) + OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**5.** When the equation below is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, what is the coefficient of water?

\_\_ H~2~SO~4~(aq) + \_\_ Al(OH)~3~(s) $\rightarrow$ \_\_ Al~2~(SO~4~)~3~(aq) + \_\_ H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 2\
b)\ 3\
c)\ 4\
d)\ 6\
e)\ 12

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**6.** Which reaction is an **oxidation–reduction** reaction?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ CaCO~3~(s) + 2HCl(aq) $\rightarrow$ CaCl~2~(aq) + H~2~O(l) + CO~2~(g)\
b)\ HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ NaCl(aq) + H~2~O(l)\
c)\ AgNO~3~(aq) + NaCl(aq) $\rightarrow$ AgCl(s) + NaNO~3~(aq)\
d)\ 2Mg(s) + O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2MgO(s)\
e)\ BaCl~2~(aq) + Na~2~SO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ BaSO~4~(s) + 2NaCl(aq)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 1\
b)\ 2\
c)\ 3\
d)\ 4\
e)\ 6

**8.** For Mg(s) + CuCl~2~(aq) $\rightarrow$ MgCl~2~(aq) + Cu(s), which statement is correct?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Each Mg atom loses 1 electron and each Cu^2+^ ion gains 1 electron\
b)\ Each Mg atom loses 2 electrons and each Cu^2+^ ion gains 2 electrons; Cl^−^ is unchanged\
c)\ No electrons are transferred; this is a double-displacement reaction\
d)\ Each Mg atom gains 2 electrons and each Cu^2+^ ion loses 2 electrons\
e)\ The Cl^−^ ions lose electrons to the magnesium

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**9.** Two **nonmetals** react. According to the course, how can you tell at this point that the reaction is an oxidation–reduction reaction?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ All the coefficients in the balanced equation are 1\
b)\ O~2~ appears as a reactant or a product\
c)\ An ionic compound forms\
d)\ A precipitate forms\
e)\ Water is one of the products

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

\needspace{9\baselineskip}

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
